description: Calculate the d-band center of a pseudomorphic Pt monolayer overlayer on Cu(111).
user_prompt: Build a Cu(111) surface slab and deposit a pseudomorphic monolayer of Pt on top of it (a full Pt overlayer coherent with the Cu lattice). Extract the d-band center (in eV relative to the Fermi level) from the Pt overlayer atoms' d-orbital projected DOS and report the final value.

references: Ruban, Hammer, Stoltze, Skriver, and Norskov, J. Mol. Catal. A: Chem. 115, 421-429 (1997).
method.modeling: Use a Cu(111) slab with one full pseudomorphic Pt monolayer overlayer held coherent with the Cu in-plane lattice. Project the DOS on the Pt overlayer atoms only.
method.rationale: Ruban et al. list pseudomorphic overlayer shifts relative to the clean elemental close-packed-surface value: clean Pt(111) is -2.25 eV and the Pt overlayer on Cu shift is -1.15 eV, giving epsilon_d = -3.40 eV. Their epsilon_d is the full d-DOS centroid relative to E_F, matching the benchmark full_d_band_centers_rel_fermi_eV convention. The coherent Cu lattice is essential because compressive strain plus Cu ligand effects drive the Pt d-band below clean Pt(111). The 0.4 eV absolute tolerance covers the gap between Ruban's LMTO-ASA/LDA, non-magnetic, unrelaxed overlayer model and a relaxed VASP/PBE/PAW slab.
